articles.title: Why Do We Need Sleep?
articles.dek: Are you tired at school? Your bed may have the answer.
paras: Do you feel tired at school? Is it hard to get up in the morning? Maybe you are not sleeping enough. Why do we need sleep? Let's find out.
Doctors say that teenagers need eight to ten hours of sleep every night. That is more than many adults need. Some students sleep only five or six hours. They should go to bed earlier.

Sleep is not just rest. When you sleep, your body is still working. Good sleep helps your brain. You can think clearly and your memory gets better. It also helps your mood. You feel less stressed and more friendly the next day.

Sleep helps your body, too. People who sleep well get ill less often. Their hearts are healthier, too. Many people also feel they have more energy for sport and games. If you want to play well on Saturday, you should sleep well on Friday.

How can you sleep better? Here is some simple advice. You should go to bed and get up at the same time every day. You should turn off your phone or tablet at least thirty minutes before bed. You shouldn't drink cola or coffee in the evening. Your bedroom should be quiet and cool.

Some students stay up late to finish homework or watch videos. They shouldn't do this too often. A tired brain works slowly, so homework takes longer. Tonight, try one small change. Tell a friend about it. Then you can help each other.

Do you ever study late the night before a test? Many students do. But it is not a good idea. You should study a little every day. Then you can sleep well before the test, and your brain will be ready.

articles.title: A Present for Dad
articles.dek: Lena has a plan, but she needs a present. Can Jack help?
paras: Hi Jack, Guess what? It's Dad's birthday on Saturday! We're going to have a small party at home. Mum is going to make a big chocolate cake, and I'm going to decorate the room. I want to buy Dad a present, but I don't know what to get. Can you help me? Love, Lena

Hi Lena, Great news! What about a nice scarf or a good book? Last year I bought my dad a wallet, and he loved it. This afternoon I'm meeting my friend Omar at the shopping centre. We're going to look for a new football shirt for me. Why don't you come with us? We're meeting at the main door at two o'clock. Jack

Hi Jack, Thanks, I'd love to come! I'm going to bring my savings. I have twenty-five pounds, but I'm not going to spend it all. I also need a card and some paper to wrap the present. I'm going to ask a shop assistant for help, too. After shopping, are we going to have lunch? I'm going to eat a big pizza! See you at two. Love, Lena

Hi Lena, Good idea! Omar isn't going to eat pizza because he's visiting his grandma at four. He's going to leave early, so we are going to have a quick lunch. I'm going to try on the football shirt first. Then we're going to look at scarves and books together. Bring a bag, because it's going to be heavy! Jack

Hi Jack, Perfect! I'm going to wear my red coat, so you can find me easily. It's going to rain this afternoon, so I'm also taking an umbrella. Thank you for your help. Dad is going to be so happy! Love, Lena

articles.title: The Late Bus
articles.dek: The bus does not come, and today is a very important day.
paras: On Monday morning, Ravi ran to the bus stop. It was raining. His bag was heavy because his science project was inside. The school bus usually came at 7:45, but today it did not come.

His friend Sofia was waiting there, too. “The bus is late,” she said. “We'll be late for school. Mr Brown won't be happy.” Ravi looked at his watch. It was ten past eight. “Maybe the bus won't come at all,” he said.

Then an old man spoke to them. “The road is closed,” he said. “There was an accident near the bridge. The buses won't come today.” Sofia felt worried. Today was the day of the science fair. Ravi's project was very important.
“I'll call my mum,” said Ravi. “She'll drive us.” But his phone was dead. Sofia gave him hers. Ravi's mum did not answer. “She's at work,” he said sadly. “She won't hear the phone.”

“Let's walk,” said Sofia. “It'll take forty minutes. I'll carry your bag for a while.” “Thanks, but I'll carry it myself. It's my project,” said Ravi. They walked fast through the rain. The old man shouted, “You'll be wet, but you'll get there!”

They arrived at nine thirty. Their teacher was standing at the door. “Where were you?” he asked. They told him the story. Mr Brown smiled. “I'm glad you came. The fair starts at ten, so you won't miss it. I'll find you a towel.” Ravi's project won second prize, and Sofia clapped the loudest.
